chapter: Haiti, Artie Shaw and Los Angeles work
title: Touring Haiti with Budd Johnson and Billy Taylor
summary: Six weeks in Haiti with Johnson, Taylor, Lloyd Trotman, Charlie Smith and Kenny Dorham, living in a mountain town with voodoo drums at night.

blocks.x: He had his own group, and he worked with Earl Hines, worked with another band by -- I think it was Jesse Stone. And I went to Haiti with Bud Johnson, and -- around the middle forties, say between '46 and '48 I think around the time -- and stayed for six weeks. And in this

band was Billy Taylor, the bass player was Lloyd Trotman and the drummer was Charlie Smith, marvelous drummer, and Kenny Durham. They had a centennial this year and Marion Anderson was there also. It was a wonderful experience but at night it was a drag because -- we lived in a little town called Patientville. It's about 12 miles, almost straight up the --
You were saying when the phone rang that you lived in a little town called what?

P-e-t-i-o-n I think, v-i-l-l-e. Yeah. But it's like a little resort town, it's about 12 miles from Port Au Prince and right up in the mountains. At night you hear these voodoo drums all night long, just -- and you don't see anything. That is the darkest place in the world. You know, we would sit there and want to get to town and we couldn't get down this mountain.

Well, no, we didn't -- actually we didn't have any transportation at this time of night, you know. So we were just stuck up here, but it was just gorgeous country, beautiful country. A lot of poverty. But musically it was very good because as you know Billy Taylor was a superb pianist, and Bud and Kenny Durham. Well, it was just a good band.
